How this atlas works

Six temperament families: the four humours in the square (A top-left opposite D), plus E competence and F mystical below. Every square has designed axes — the italic labels on its edges name what left↔right and top↔bottom mean, so a trait's position inside its square tells you where it sits on those two dimensions. Between squares, bold-bordered transition bands hold blends (inner half) and unity traits fusing two families (outer third); diagonal strips hold cross-quadrant pairs; the centre hub holds 3+-family combiners.

Tap a trait: its profile opens and orange spokes fan out to its eight most semantically similar traits anywhere on the map, each spoke labelled with the correlation (thicker = stronger). Tap an adjective: gold threads light every trait using that word — thread thickness shows how many families a word spans. Both selections stay visible at every zoom level, so zoom out to see a word or trait's full reach.

Zooming: labels keep a constant readable size while the map grows beneath them. Medium zoom shows major-trait labels only; deeper shows all traits and adjectives (staggered above/below their dots); deepest expands names to full text — dense areas untangle as you go.

Top bar: Temperament / Hormone switch colour views; Confidence fades each trait by how well its neighbours match its true semantic neighbours (dashed red ring = approximate placement — check its profile). ‹ back retraces your views; reset clears and zooms out; find… searches traits and adjectives.

Guide tab: fit filters (how strongly traits belong to a family or named cluster, in 20% bands), the cluster map spotlight, and node display toggles. Connectivity / Theorists / Field tabs browse by connections, author, or discipline.

Jumping around: the correlated-trait rows inside any profile take you straight to that trait, and tapping a theorist name (▸) lights every trait they described.

Adjective pills: in any profile, blue pills are words whose traits all sit inside one family/community; orange pills are bridge words used by traits in two or more regions — the connective tissue of the map. Tap any pill to light its full reach.

Meaning links: tapping a word also shows its nearest words by meaning — dashed teal links on the map and a matching “Nearest in meaning” list in the panel (each row = one teal link, with its similarity, or syn for a dictionary synonym) — computed from semantic distance in the underlying embedding, plus dictionary synonyms in “Synonyms (in chart)”. This connects near-identical words (empathic ≈ empathetic) even when no single trait uses both.

🔒 Lock: freezes the profile you are reading so clicks on the map stop changing it — useful when you want to trace a thread or a spoke across the chart without losing your place. Everything inside the panel still works, and zoom and pan are unaffected. Leave it unlocked unless you specifically want that, since while it is on the map will not respond to clicks at all.

Same name, different theorist: many words are used by more than one system — Klages and Reiss both describe an “Independence,” Cattell and Tomkins both an “Anger.” Each keeps its own profile and its own position, so twins that mean the same thing sit almost on top of each other while twins that don’t sit far apart. Any profile with a namesake lists it under Same name, other theorists.

◈ Convergence: recolours every trait by how many independent systems describe it the same way — purple = convergent core (four or more systems agree), blue = triple, amber = pair, grey = outlier (no other system matches it closely). Every profile now names its cluster, the systems in it, and can light the whole cluster up.

⇆ Compare: click a trait — or lasso a whole area with the ◌ tool — to set an anchor (blue); each later click or lasso fills whichever side is marked ◉ — use the replace this side buttons to aim at the left or right card. Traits and regions mix freely: trait vs trait, region vs region, or trait vs region. Shared adjectives highlight in violet, and near matches lists semantically equivalent word pairs the two traits don’t literally share. ◌ Lasso: draw around any area to harvest its cumulative adjective list, sorted by how distinctive each word is for that region versus the whole atlas (or toggle to plain frequency); while the tool is on, tap traits to add or remove them.

Reading a square’s axes: the italic edge labels are that family’s two designed dimensions — in B, for instance, further right = more dominant, further down = more image-hungry.

Text too small? Use your browser’s own zoom — View › Zoom In (or Ctrl/⌘ and +) — until everything is a size you can read comfortably. The whole atlas scales with it.

What the marks mean
  • spokes — a trait’s eight nearest traits
  • threads — traits sharing a tapped word
  • teal dashes — nearest words by meaning
  • violet dashes — the compare link
  • compare anchor (left card)
  • compare candidate (right card)
